raw:
“I’ll see you tomorrow,” you tell Owen.

“Friday, probably,” he says, tucking the tape measure into his pocket. “I’m out tomorrow morning. Have a good walk.”

You leave by the front doors and head down Harbour Street toward the harbour. The tide has drawn back from the inner wall, exposing dark weeded stones beneath the moored fishing boats. A gull worries at something in the gutter while two men in waterproof trousers sort crates beside a van. Wind comes in off the water and catches at the mended cuff of your coat.

You follow the harbour rail as far as the breakwater, then turn back toward the Picture House. By the time you reach Harbour Street again, your break is nearly over; its faded frontage waits one road back from the water.
